Boston Public Schools (1) have more teachers than they need to provide instruction in core academic subjects; (2) have more teachers in the central office than in schools; (3) have more teachers with advanced degrees than in schools; and (4) have more teachers teaching in schools with high concentrations of poor and minority students than in schools with low concentrations of these students.
